reports.title: Quick Thoughts on China Immersion News
reports.headline: ASML pressured on reports China has started manufacturing ArFi tools; Wells sees NT reaction as potentially overdone pending proof of HVM viability.
reports.summary: Wells takes a wait-and-see view on reports that a state-backed CN mfr has begun producing immersion litho tools, arguing the -8% ASML move may overstate risk because CN ArFi efforts are not new and HVM placement/specs remain unproven. The key debate is whether domestic tools can scale beyond limited shipments and materially impair ASML's China position; Wells previously sized a full China ArFi restriction at ~€3B, or ~5% of its 2027 ASML rev est.
important_observations: Reported CN ArFi shipments of 5 tools in 2026 and up to 20 in 2027 are small vs Wells' est of ~170 ASML immersion tool shipments in 2027.
20 tools in 2027 could still matter at the fab level: Wells notes a 45k wspm 10nm F/L fab needs ~19 ArFi tools, while a 100k wspm 1Ynm DRAM fab needs ~15.
The investment question is less whether CN can build ArFi tools and more whether overlay/throughput can approach ASML NXT-class tools and support HVM.
Prior SMEE delivery to SMIC in early 2025 was reportedly targeted at 28nm, suggesting capability may remain behind leading-edge ASML immersion use cases.
Export restriction risk remains active: ASML already cannot ship NXT:2000i to CN, while the MATCH Act would seek broader immersion restrictions.

Reported customers include SMIC, Hua Hong and CXMT, with deliveries expected this yr.

reports.title: SK Hynix: Debates but significant growth ahead - OW
reports.headline: Barclays switches SKHY coverage to ADRs at OW with $330 PT, arguing DRAM/HBM tightness worsens into 2027 and cash generation can extend the equity story beyond ASP gains.
reports.summary: Barclays initiates/switches SKHY ADR coverage at OW with a $330 PT, seeing 117% upside from the Jul 13 close. The note addresses investor debates from US marketing: whether memory pricing is structurally different this cycle, whether LTAs protect downside, China supply risk, HBM competition, and whether a buyback thesis can replace ASP-led upside. Barclays’ core variant view is that supply/demand tightness deteriorates in 2027 and improves only modestly in 2028, while SKHY sustains HBM leadership and generates cash equal to >40% of current mkt cap by YE27, enabling potential buybacks even as ASP growth slows.
important_observations: Investor skepticism remains high on whether this memory cycle is different; Barclays agrees a downcycle eventually comes but thinks unprecedented AI demand can extend the upcycle longer than prior cycles.
Supply additions are viewed as back-end loaded, so Barclays expects DRAM demand growth of 35% y/y in 2027 vs bit supply growth of 20%, keeping the industry tight.
LTAs improve visibility but are not seen by investors or Barclays as sufficient protection in a material downturn.
Barclays expects HBM pricing to step up 70-80% from start-2027 for SKHY, tied to conventional DRAM pricing levels, though LT HBM pricing risk remains.
SKHY is expected to hold 50%+ HBM share for several years; Samsung’s HBM4 tech edge is expected to be neutralized at HBM4E.
The story may shift from ASP growth to bit shipment growth and buybacks; Barclays models cash nearly >40% of current market cap by YE27.
US front-end manufacturing could help narrow SKHY’s discount to MU.

reports.headline: 2Q26 results showed stable underlying demand but payer mix pressure drove a FY26 EBITDA guide reset; focus shifts to 2H26 util seasonality and mix.
reports.summary: GS frames HCA's 2Q26 as less about headline results, which were preannounced, and more about the mix-driven EBITDA reset. Rev and EBITDA benefited from stronger pricing tied to FL Medicaid directed payments, but this was offset by weaker ACA Exchange vols, a nearly one-for-one rise in uninsured vols, higher self-pay mix, and softer surgical activity. Underlying demand stayed resilient, with same-facility equivalent admissions, Medicare vols, insured vols ex-Exchange, and ER visits all growing, so the key debate is whether 2H26 seasonality and elective surgery weakness persist or stabilize.

Underlying demand remained stable: same-facility equivalent admissions +2.7%, insured vols ex-Exchange +3.2%, Medicare vols +3.6%, ER visits +3.6%.
Surgical volumes were a notable soft spot, especially elective procedures, tied to Exchange volume declines and broader affordability pressure.
Medicaid supplemental payment outlook improved, but the benefit partly reflects payments already received in 1H26 rather than a stronger forward run-rate.

reports.headline: Jefferies remains bullish into APP Q2 despite trimming 2H26/2027 ests, citing positive e-comm checks, solid gaming ROAS, and valuation near 18-mo lows.
reports.summary: Jefferies previews APP Q2 positively, arguing the stock can work with a modest Q2 rev beat and Q3 guide for mid-to-high-single-digit q/q growth. E-comm survey data was incrementally better vs Q1, with APP gaining share and 4Q25 onboarded customers ramping spend, though new-customer GA ramp appears slower than prior expectations. Jefferies cuts 2H26 and 2027 rev/EBITDA ests by ~3%, but remains above cons, reiterates Buy and $700 PT, and keeps APP as a top pick.
important_observations: APP FY2 EV/EBITDA at ~16x is near 18-mo lows while shares are down 36% YTD, creating what Jefferies sees as a valuation floor setup.
Investor debate centers on whether e-comm GA opening drives a 2H26 inflection; Jefferies now sees less new-customer contribution but better spend ramp from existing advertisers.
Bulls want Q2 rev 7%-8% q/q, or $50-$60M above the guide high end, plus Q3 guide of 8%+ q/q rev growth.
Bears expect only in-line/slight Q2 upside and a more typical 4%-6% q/q Q3 rev guide if e-comm GA ramp remains slow.
Jefferies still sees 25%+ LT rev growth supported by 2026 new customers ramping into 2027.
new_data: 2Q26 e-comm survey showed APP gaining the most ad-budget share among peers from 4Q25 to 2026, +169 bps among current APP advertisers.
E-comm checks were incrementally positive vs Q1, with rising ROAS and APP maintaining top-3 share position.
Gaming checks remain solid on APP ROAS, but share trends appear less positive than Q1, implying lower odds of an outsized Q2 beat.
Usage/commentary on APP gen AI products improved vs muted Q1 feedback.
4Q25 onboarding customers were more represented in the survey sample and appear to be ramping spend similarly to prior cohorts.
management_insights: Mgmt commentary on opening the platform to a general audience implies incremental gains rather than a sharp 2H inflection.
Mgmt disclosed an e-comm model enhancement that drove Apr to a new e-comm record, which bulls view as underappreciated.
Key mgmt qtr focus will be validation of e-comm GA ramp, existing-advertiser spend trends, and Q3 guide tone.
estimate_changes: Lowered 2H26 rev ests, with 3Q/4Q q/q growth now 8.6%/18% vs prior 14%/19%.
Kept 3Q/4Q gaming rev growth unchanged at 8% q/q each.
Lowered 2026 rev and EBITDA ests by ~3%.
Lowered 2027 rev and EBITDA ests by ~3%.
Reiterated Buy and $700 PT.

evidence_quality: Survey-based: 2Q26 Jefferies e-comm advertiser survey supports share-gain and ROAS observations; useful but sample details are limited in extracted text.
Channel checks: gaming and e-comm checks provide NT demand/ROAS read-throughs, but appear qualitative and not fully quantified.
Company-reported guidance/results: Q2/Q3 setup is anchored to APP guide framework and prior company disclosures, including Apr e-comm model enhancement commentary.
Analyst model work: estimate cuts and valuation rely on Jefferies forecast assumptions and EV/EBITDA framework; useful for street setup but partly analyst inference.
risks_or_watch_items: Q3 guide below 8% q/q rev growth could reinforce bear case that e-comm GA ramp is slower than hoped.
New e-comm customer adds may remain a headwind even if existing advertisers ramp spend.
Gaming share trends less positive than Q1 could limit Q2 beat magnitude.
Privacy changes from Apple, Google, or regulators could pressure targeting and ad performance.
Mobile gaming spending or ad demand weakness could impair APP growth algorithm.
